quickAnswer: Sterling ranks 1st of the 50 towns we serve for fuel oil heating: 73.0% of occupied homes burn it, while only 4.4% use utility gas. The town has its own municipal electric utility, which changes how heat pump rebates work.
body: ## Number one for oil

No town on our list leans on fuel oil harder than Sterling. The Census Bureau's 2022 American Community Survey (ACS) counts 2,525 occupied homes on oil or kerosene, 73.0% of the total, against 36.5% for the middle town. Electricity heats 270 homes (7.8%), wood heats 269 (7.8%), bottled or tank gas heats 202 (5.8%), and utility gas heats only 151 (4.4%), which ranks 49th of 50.

With figures like these, a replacement often comes down to a new oil system against a heat pump. According to Wikipedia, Eversource provides natural gas service in Sterling, so gas is worth asking about at your own address, though 151 gas homes suggest a main will not reach every street.
## Few vacant homes, few apartments, mostly detached houses

Sterling has 3,477 housing units and only 16 of them are vacant, a vacancy rate of 0.5%. That is 49th of 50, against 3.6% for the middle town. Detached single-family houses are 84.1% of the stock (13th-highest), and just 249 units, 7.2%, sit in multi-unit buildings (43rd). Owners occupy 3,075 households (88.8%) and renters 386 (11.2%). The median owner-occupied home is worth $423,300, 41st of 50 and well under the middle town's $579,150.

Of the 3,477 units, 2,923 are detached houses and 305 are attached townhouse units. Buildings of three or four units number 119, buildings of five or more number 114, and two-unit buildings number 16. The count includes no mobile homes. Sterling ranks 39th of 50 for its share of renter households, well below the middle town's 16.4%.
## A town split by the interstate, with no sewer

Interstate 190 cuts Sterling in half, and Routes 12, 62, 140 and 110 cross it. The town covers 31.7 square miles, 30.6 of them land. Town water comes from six groundwater wells, while the more rural parts remain on private wells. There are no town sewer services, and all houses have private septic systems. A well and a septic field are two things any outdoor equipment has to be placed around.

Sterling began as the Second Parish of Lancaster, was commonly called Chocksett, and was incorporated as its own town in 1781. The first settlers arrived in 1720, and their family names (Beman, Sawyer, Houghton and Osgood) are still reflected in the names of Sterling's oldest roads. In housing terms, 511 homes (14.7%) date from 1939 or earlier, and 55.0% were built before 1980, below the 57.2% of the middle town. The median home was built in 1977.
## What a municipal electric utility means for rebates

Sterling is one of 41 communities in the state with its own municipal electric light company, the Sterling Municipal Light Department. Because the department, and not National Grid, is the utility, heat pump rebate rules differ from those in most of the 50 towns, and the department itself is the first call for most owners. Our [heat pump page](/cities/sterling/heat-pumps-ductless-mini-splits) lays out what depends on what.

In the fall of 2016 the Light Department broke ground on what it calls the first utility-scale energy storage facility in Massachusetts. It can keep the dispatch center and police station powered for up to twelve days in an outage. The department also runs a municipal broadband service called Sterling LAMB.

faq.q: Why do so many Sterling homes burn oil?
faq.a: The Census Bureau reports the number, 73.0% of occupied homes, but not the reason. What it means for you is practical: oil is the starting point for most replacements, so the real comparison is a new oil system against a heat pump, with gas considered only if a main reaches your street.

faq.q: Does Sterling's municipal utility change who I call about a heat pump?
faq.a: For rebate questions, yes. The Sterling Municipal Light Department is the electric utility, one of 41 municipal ones in the state, so ask it about its own heat pump program first. Whether any Mass Save rebate applies depends on how the home is heated. Confirm terms at masssave.com before planning around a figure.

faq.q: Is natural gas available on my Sterling street?
faq.a: Wikipedia says Eversource provides natural gas service in Sterling, and 151 homes (4.4%) use it. Whether a main passes your address is something the gas company can answer. If none does, oil or a heat pump are the usual choices.

faq.q: Are Sterling's houses old enough to need insulation or duct work?
faq.a: It depends on the house. The median home dates to 1977, and 511 homes go back to 1939 or earlier. Insulation and air leakage vary a great deal between eras, which is why the home's heating load is worked out before any system is quoted. A home among the 685 built in 2000 or later sits at the newer end of that range.

heating-installation-repair.quickAnswer: Oil heats 2,525 Sterling homes, the highest share of the 50 towns, while 151 use utility gas. A boiler or furnace replacement here is mostly a choice between another oil system and a heat pump.
body: ## Replacing equipment in the top oil town

Sterling holds first place for fuel oil among the 50 towns, with 73.0% of occupied homes against a middle-town figure of 36.5%. Electricity heats 270 homes and wood heats 269, nearly level with each other. Another 202 use tank gas and 44 use other fuels or coal. Gas from a main reaches 151 homes, which is the 49th-highest share.
### What each path involves

A new oil boiler can keep the tank, the chimney and much of the pipework, so the work is largely a unit swap. A heat pump removes the burner, and some houses keep a boiler for the coldest days. Moving to gas needs a main at the street, a new gas line and a venting plan.
### Gas work and the permit

For gas equipment, only licensed plumbers and gas fitters may pull the permit in Massachusetts, and a new furnace or boiler normally goes through a final inspection. The town's building department can explain its filing steps.
### Fit with the house

Sterling's median home was built in 1977, and 917 homes date from 1960 through 1979. Heating loops sized for an old boiler may not suit a new unit, so the home's heating load is assessed before a system is quoted, not copied from the nameplate.
### Renters in a small group

Sterling has 386 renter households. Under the state sanitary code, a rented unit has to stay at 68 F or above from 7 a.m. to 11 p.m., and 64 F overnight, through the heating season. The lease decides who pays for heat, and the default is the landlord. This is general information, not legal advice.
### When heat stops

For an outage at night call (508) 786-8755. Emergency calls are taken 24 hours a day, and written estimates are free before work begins. The [Sterling overview](/cities/sterling) has the broader housing picture, including the 16 vacant units out of 3,477.

faq.q: Is a new oil boiler still the usual choice in Sterling?
faq.a: With 2,525 oil homes it is the most common replacement path, and the existing tank and chimney often stay in use. It is still worth comparing against a heat pump, particularly if the old boiler is near the end of its life and the house is reasonably tight.

faq.q: Can I convert from oil to gas in Sterling?
faq.a: Only where a main runs past the property. Eversource provides gas service in town, but just 151 homes use it. Ask the gas company first, then price the conversion against an oil replacement and a heat pump before committing to any work.

faq.q: Should I keep my wood stove as a second heat source?
faq.a: Wood heats 269 Sterling homes, 7.8%, so many owners already treat it as a backup. A stove only helps if the chimney and flue are sound, so have them checked before depending on one through a long cold stretch.

air-conditioning-installation-repair.quickAnswer: Detached houses make up 84.1% of Sterling's housing, and only 249 units sit in multi-unit buildings. Central air suits houses with usable ducts, and ductless suits the rest.
body: ## Cooling mostly detached houses

Sterling is 13th of 50 for share of detached single-family homes. Counting 2,923 of its 3,477 units, they set the pattern for cooling work, with the 305 attached townhouse units and 249 multi-unit homes making up the rest. A detached house generally allows a condenser at ground level.
### Ducts or no ducts

Central air needs duct runs to every room it serves. Houses with forced-air heat may already have some, while those heated by baseboard or radiators may not. A house built before central air was common may need new ducts opened into walls or ceilings, which is where a ductless system can be the simpler route.
### How a mini-split works

An outdoor unit connects to one or more indoor heads through a thin line set. Each head cools its own room, and the equipment can heat in winter too. The [heat pump page](/cities/sterling/heat-pumps-ductless-mini-splits) covers how that works with the town's municipal utility.
### Electric heat and summer power

Electricity heats 270 Sterling homes, 7.8%, ranking 41st of 50. In those houses a heat pump can handle summer cooling and shift part of the winter load off resistance heat. A large new system may also mean an electrical upgrade, which is a question for the Light Department as the electric utility. Sterling's power comes from its municipal Light Department.
### Comfort and humidity

A unit that is too large cools quickly and shuts off before it removes much moisture, leaving a damp chill. Sizing should follow the house itself, including insulation, window area and orientation, and not the old unit's label. With detached houses dominating, each house gets its own calculation.
### Newer houses

The 685 homes built in 2000 or later, 19.7% of the stock, may already have ducts that can serve a central system. Of those, 202 date from 2010 or later. The 917 homes from 1960 through 1979 and the 879 from 1980 through 1999 sit in between, and their ducts, where they exist, should be checked for size before a new coil goes on.

faq.q: Can I add central air to a Sterling house with baseboard heat?
faq.a: It is possible but often costly, because duct runs have to be created. Many owners of baseboard houses choose a ductless mini-split instead, with one head per area. The choice turns on how many rooms need cooling and what the walls and attic allow.

faq.q: Is one mini-split enough for a whole house?
faq.a: Usually not for a whole house. One head can cool a single open area, such as a living room or a bedroom. Cooling several rooms takes several heads or a ducted air handler. A visit to the house shows how many zones make sense.

faq.q: What fails first on an older central air system?
faq.a: Frequently something small, such as a worn capacitor, a clogged coil or a slow refrigerant leak. A dead compressor in an old unit is a different matter and may favor replacement. Ask for the estimate in writing so the cheap fixes and the costly ones are not mixed together.

heat-pumps-ductless-mini-splits.quickAnswer: Sterling has its own municipal electric utility, so the rebate path depends on how a home heats and is a matter for the Light Department first. With 73.0% of homes on oil, most owners start there.
body: ## Rebates in a municipal electric town

Electricity here comes from the town's own Light Department, so the usual Mass Save path narrows: its heat pump rebates generally reach only homes that heat with natural gas from a Mass Save sponsor. Everyone else should ask the Light Department about its program. The [general heat pump page](/services/heat-pumps-ductless-mini-splits) lists the Mass Save terms.
### Why this matters in an oil town

Only 151 Sterling homes use gas, 4.4%, so the 2,525 on oil, 202 on tank gas and 270 on electricity sit on the other side of that line and the Light Department is their likelier contact. Eversource provides gas service in town, but a main has to reach the street first.
### Age against weatherization

One route through Mass Save's weatherization test is being built in 2000 or later, and 685 Sterling homes, 19.7%, meet that on age alone. The rest were built earlier: 879 homes are from 1980 through 1999 and 917 from 1960 through 1979. Under Mass Save rules those homes would need an assessment first; the Light Department can say what its own program asks.
### What a heat pump replaces

A heat pump displaces a delivered, burned fuel in the oil homes, a tank fuel in the 202 propane homes, and resistance heating in the 270 electric homes. The 269 wood homes are the odd group, since a stove and a heat pump can share the load.
### Resilience and the local grid

The Light Department also runs a municipal broadband service, Sterling LAMB, so one local office handles both power and part of the town's internet. For a heat pump owner the point is that a single local office is the contact on the electricity side.
### Ducts and mini-splits

Where a house has no ducts, a ductless system can still serve it. The [cooling page](/cities/sterling/air-conditioning-installation-repair) explains how mini-splits fit detached houses, which are 84.1% of Sterling's stock.

faq.q: Who do I call first about heat pump rebates in Sterling?
faq.a: Start with the Sterling Municipal Light Department, because it is the electric utility and one of only 41 municipal light companies in the state. Ask what it offers for your fuel and your house, then check masssave.com in case your situation qualifies there as well.

faq.q: Can a heat pump replace my oil boiler completely?
faq.a: In a tight, well-insulated house it can. In many others the heat pump covers most of the year while the boiler handles the coldest days. How much of the load a heat pump can carry is a heating-load question, and the answer comes before any system is quoted or ordered.

faq.q: Do wood-heat homes in Sterling suit a heat pump?
faq.a: They can. A heat pump gives steady background warmth, while a stove adds heat when someone is home to feed it. With 269 wood homes in town, the combination is worth pricing, and the stove can stay as a second source.

hvac-maintenance-tune-ups.quickAnswer: With 73.0% of Sterling homes on oil, annual burner service is the most common maintenance job in town. Wood, gas, tank gas and electric homes each need their own kind of check.
body: ## Annual service in an oil town

An oil boiler or furnace wants cleaning once a year: burner, nozzle, filter and heat exchanger, with a combustion test. With 2,525 oil homes, this is the job at the top of the list. Late summer is a common time to book it.
### Other fuels

- **Wood:** 269 homes. Chimney and flue inspection, plus a check on the stove's seals.
- **Tank gas:** 202 homes. Burner, venting and connection check.
- **Utility gas:** 151 homes. Same checks on a gas appliance.
- **Electric and heat pump:** 270 homes. Filters, coils and condensate drains.
### Equipment age and the house

The median Sterling house dates to 1977, and 879 homes come from 1980 through 1999. Boilers and furnaces in houses of those decades may have been replaced once, but the age of the unit still sets the pace for service.
### Small renter group, still on a schedule
Sterling has 386 renter households. A landlord who has the boiler serviced ahead of the first cold week has less to worry about on a no-heat call.
### The yearly habit

Owners hold 3,075 of Sterling's 3,461 occupied homes, 88.8%, so most of this work is a homeowner booking a visit for their own house. A habit that works is one visit in late summer for the heating system and one in spring for cooling. Pair the visit with a check of the fuel tank and its fill and vent lines, and with a look at the chimney if the house also burns wood.
### Unusual fuels
The ACS lists 44 Sterling homes on other fuels or coal. Those appliances do not fit a standard checklist, so tell the technician what the equipment burns when you book.
### Cooling checks
Spring is the time for air conditioners and mini-splits: a look at the outdoor unit, the coil and the drain. Keep the outdoor unit clear of leaves and snow in between.
### When not to wait

Unusual sounds, a smell of oil or smoke, and short cycling, where the equipment starts and stops every few minutes, are reasons to call early rather than wait for the yearly visit. The [air quality page](/cities/sterling/indoor-air-quality) covers what a tune-up leaves out.

faq.q: How often should my Sterling oil boiler be serviced?
faq.a: Yearly, before the heating season. Skipping a year can let soot build up, which may cut efficiency and cause a breakdown during a cold spell. A late-summer visit leaves time to order a part if something is worn.

faq.q: Does a wood stove need a tune-up?
faq.a: It needs a chimney and flue inspection, and cleaning if creosote has built up. Seals and glass should be checked too. With 269 wood-heat homes in town, a yearly look before the first fire is a sensible habit.

faq.q: Do heat pumps and mini-splits need service?
faq.a: Yes, though it is lighter than burner work. Filters need cleaning, coils and condensate drains need a look, and the outdoor unit needs clearance. Doing this once a year keeps small problems from turning into service calls.

indoor-air-quality.quickAnswer: Sterling's 3,477 homes range from 511 built in 1939 or earlier to 202 built since 2010, so air problems differ: old houses leak, newer ones are tighter. Private wells serve the rural parts of town.
body: ## Air across every era of building

By the ACS 2022 counts, Sterling has 485 homes (13.9%) from 1940 to 1959, 917 (26.4%) from 1960 to 1979, 879 (25.3%) from 1980 to 1999, and 685 (19.7%) from 2000 on. The 1960 to 1979 and 1980 to 1999 bands are each about a quarter of the stock, so most of the town sits in the middle bands.
### Older houses

Older houses tend to leak more air around windows, sills and attic floors. That can dilute some indoor pollutants, but it can also pull in dust and damp. Before renovating a very old house, ask a qualified specialist about testing for lead paint or asbestos.
### Tighter houses

A house built since 2000, which includes 685 Sterling homes, is usually tighter. A tight envelope saves energy, though it also traps humidity and cooking fumes unless fresh air comes in somewhere. Exhaust fans that vent outdoors do more work in such a house.
### Wells and humidifiers

Town water in Sterling comes from six groundwater wells, and the more rural parts rely on private wells. A humidifier on a private well can build up mineral scale, so ask about pads and upkeep before buying.
### Wood smoke and combustion

Wood heats 269 Sterling homes. A stove that is poorly vented or fed damp wood can put smoke and fine particles into the house, so a sound flue matters. A carbon monoxide alarm on each floor is a cheap safeguard for oil, tank gas and wood alike.
### Basements and damp air

Wherever a basement stays damp, a dehumidifier sized to the space can protect stored items and reduce musty air. Sealing obvious gaps and venting dryers outdoors help too. The fix depends on where the moisture comes from, so find the source before buying equipment.
### Filters and ducts
Before upgrading a filter, confirm the blower can pull air through it. Duct cleaning is a job for visible dirt or mold. The [tune-up page](/cities/sterling/hvac-maintenance-tune-ups) covers upkeep.

faq.q: Is the air in an older Sterling house worse than in a new one?
faq.a: Not necessarily. Old houses leak, which helps ventilation but admits dust and damp. Tighter newer houses keep moisture and cooking fumes inside. In either kind of house the source of the problem has to be found before the fix is chosen.

faq.q: Do I need my ducts cleaned?
faq.a: Not as a routine. Visible dirt, mold, or a renovation that stirred up the runs are the usual reasons for cleaning. Many houses never need it, and a look at the whole system, including filters and returns, comes before any decision.

faq.q: Does private well water affect a humidifier?
faq.a: It can. Hard well water may leave mineral scale on pads and in the tank, which means more cleaning and sometimes replacement parts. Ask about maintenance before choosing a unit, and test the water if you are unsure of its hardness, since hardness varies from one well to another.
